## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all user-visible states for the primary flow explicitly specified? [Completeness, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK002 Are role permissions and denied-access outcomes defined for every protected action? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK003 Are required data sources and ownership boundaries documented for every feature surface? [Completeness, Spec §Requirements]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK004 Are vague terms such as "fast", "intuitive", or "prominent" quantified with concrete criteria? [Clarity, Ambiguity]
- [ ] CHK005 Are success criteria written so an independent reviewer can determine pass/fail objectively? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK006 Are all navigation entry and exit points named with explicit routes or product locations? [Clarity, Spec §User Flow & Navigation]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK007 Are functional requirements consistent with the acceptance scenarios for each user story? [Consistency, Spec §Functional Requirements]
- [ ] CHK008 Are prototype, spec, and stated requirement source differences documented instead of conflicting silently? [Consistency, Spec §Input & Generation Rules]
- [ ] CHK009 Are shared terms used consistently across user stories, requirements, entities, and success criteria? [Consistency, Spec §Requirements]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK010 Does the spec cover empty, loading, error, and partial-data states where they are user-visible? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK011 Does the spec define negative and recovery paths for failed user actions or unavailable dependencies? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK012 Are responsive, accessibility, and localization expectations documented for affected UI surfaces? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK013 Are performance targets expressed as measurable thresholds for affected critical paths? [NFR, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK014 Are security and privacy requirements explicit when user data, permissions, or privileged answers are involved? [NFR, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK015 Are observability or audit requirements specified when the feature changes operationally significant workflows? [NFR, Gap]

## Constitution-Specific Requirement Gates

- [ ] CHK016 If task type behavior changes, does the spec require config-driven registry/schema/frozen task config rather than hardcoded task logic? [Principle: II, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK017 If annotator-facing data is affected, does the spec explicitly prohibit ground-truth, scoring key, answer path, or hidden-label exposure? [Principle: III, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK018 If UI is affected, does the spec reference approved design tokens/prototype expectations and document any intentional deviation? [Principle: VII, Spec §Interface Definition]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK019 Are upstream/downstream dependencies and assumptions recorded with validation expectations? [Assumption, Spec §Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK020 Are out-of-scope items or deferred decisions explicitly listed so they cannot be mistaken for requirements? [Completeness, Gap]
- [ ] CHK021 Are requirements traceable enough that tasks can be mapped back to user stories or FR IDs? [Traceability, Spec §Functional Requirements]

## Notes

- Check off completed items: `[x]`
- Add inline comments for any findings or issues
- Link to relevant resources or documents
- Items are numbered consecutively for easy reference
- At least 80% of generated checklist items must include a traceability reference such as `[Spec §FR-001]`, `[Gap]`, `[Ambiguity]`, `[Conflict]`, or `[Assumption]`
- Do not include items that require running code, executing tests, clicking UI, verifying API status codes, or confirming implementation behavior
